metadata.changelog: v3: gold_chunk_ids and anchor_phrases manually curated by a clinician to align with actual guideline content. Chunks selected from the ingested CSV based on case risk factors, active guideline, and treatment decisions. Anchor phrases reflect key terms in those chunks. | v4: gold_chunk_ids expanded via retrieval pooling across ablation/model eval runs (ablation.csv, ablation__1_.csv, model1.csv, model1__1_.csv) - chunks consistently retrieved by the live retrieval system across arms/backbones were manually reviewed against each case's active guideline, risk drivers, and contraindication/trend context, and added to gold_chunk_ids only where still clinically relevant to that case (same active_guideline source, correct clinical scenario/severity tier). WHO-guideline retrieval candidates were reviewed and excluded from this pass: WHO's multi-tier structure (critical illness vs clinical severe infection/PSBI vs pathogen-specific regimens for meningitis/staphylococcal infection) made keyword-level matches unreliable indicators of true relevance, so WHO gold_chunk_ids/anchor_phrases are unchanged from v3. anchor_phrases extended correspondingly with representative terms drawn from newly added chunks. | v4.1: added 3 further manually-verified chunks (NICE_pg74 CRP-alone caution for CRP-driven cases; AAP multivariate risk-assessment validation chunk for the two AAP LOW-risk cases; AAP intraamniotic-infection definition chunk for an AAP HIGH-risk fever/chorio case) after re-reviewing single-concept-hit candidates by hand. | v4.2: closed the remaining anchor_phrases gaps -- 9 distinct gold chunks (recurring across 26 of 30 cases) had no anchor_phrases entry matching their own text (verified by direct substring check against chunks_ingested_1_.csv), even though all were manually confirmed on-topic (treatment duration, clinical-signs-based EOS approach, categorical risk thresholds, WHO regimen-comparison RCT outcomes, antibiotic-decision principles, referral emphasis). Added one verified, verbatim-present anchor phrase per chunk rather than removing any gold_chunk_ids. anchor_grounding_recall ceiling (fraction of a case's own anchor_phrases findable in its own gold_chunk_ids' text) is now 100% for all 30 cases, up from 30/30 cases already >0% but 26/30 short of 100% before this pass. | v6: audited the 100-case dataset directly (not re-confirming the same checks -- looking for what wasn't tested yet). Found a real generation bug: the original substitution logic matched bare numbers by value, so when one field's OLD value coincidentally equaled a DIFFERENT field's NEWLY-jittered value (confirmed case: base cp_case_006's wbc_count was 18.5, and an unrelated field jittered to 18.5 too), a later substitution pass would silently overwrite an already-correct driver reason with the wrong field's value (cp_case_044 ended up with 'ROM 20.2h' while patient.rom_hours said 18.5). Rewrote substitution to be context-anchored (matches 'ROM {n}h', 'CRP {n} mg/L', 'Maternal temp {n}C', 'urine output {n} mL/kg/hr', 'creatinine {n} mg/dL' specifically -- the only 5 fields ever echoed into prose text, verified by direct search) instead of matching bare numbers, which eliminates the collision class entirely, and regenerated all 70 variants from the clean 30. Also checked: 6 exact-duplicate patient-vitals pairs exist, but all are among the ORIGINAL 30 base cases (pre-existing, not introduced by generation) -- some pairs look like deliberate same-presentation-different-guideline test design (e.g. identical vitals scored under AAP in one case, NICE in another), others look like unintentional redundancy in the original 30; flagging rather than altering clinician-authored case framing unilaterally. Investigated the total_score-vs-driver-points-sum mismatch flagged by the prior audit (91/100 cases): traced to the ORIGINAL 30 cases already (27/30 mismatched before any generation), and confirmed even the reported layer1/2/3 subscores don't sum to total_score in a simple additive way (e.g. cp_case_001: layer sums 4+2+2=8, but total_score=7) -- consistent with the harness's own documented admission that real EOSCAL scoring happens in a separate app not available here, and total_score/layer scores are its (undocumented, non-additive) output rather than a simple function of the driver points list shown. Did NOT force total_score = sum(points) -- that would mean overwriting a real (if opaque) score with fabricated arithmetic with no clinical basis, worse than leaving the known limitation documented. Fixed a real, separate issue instead: 6 penicillin_allergy cases (2 base + 4 derived) had proposed_drugs=['ampicillin','gentamicin'] -- a penicillin-class drug proposed for a documented penicillin allergy -- even though antibiotic_plan.regimen already correctly said 'IV clindamycin (per documented penicillin allergy)'; proposed_drugs just wasn't synced to match. Fixed by syncing to ['clindamycin','gentamicin']. Note: for the AAP cases in this set (cp_case_019/073/074), clindamycin itself has zero verbatim grounding anywhere in the AAP corpus (checked directly) -- AAP's source material has no penicillin-allergy-alternative guidance at all, consistent with why the 'penicillin allergy' anchor phrase was already dropped for this case in an earlier round. Syncing the field fixes the immediate contraindication error but doesn't manufacture guideline grounding that doesn't exist in the source; flagging as a pre-existing content gap, not something further edits here can close. Re-ran the full audit suite after all fixes: 0 ungrounded anchors, 0 nonexistent chunk refs, 0 driver-reason/patient-dict mismatches, 0 remaining penicillin-class drugs in allergy cases, 100/100 cases load via the real harness loader, 200/200 smoke-test retrieval calls succeed.

CLINICAL SUMMARY:
Neonate assessed under NICE NG195 (2026-amended) scoring 7 points (High Risk (Red), ~12.0 per 1000 estimated EOS probability). Key findings: Maternal GBS colonization (GBS positive); Prolonged rupture of membranes (ROM 25.0h (>=18h)); Maternal intrapartum fever (Maternal temp 38.5C); Respiratory distress (Moderate respiratory distress); Elevated CRP (CRP 28.2 mg/L).

RISK ANALYSIS:
Risk stratification under NICE places this infant in the High Risk (Red) category. Contributing risk factors span maternal/peripartum, clinical, and laboratory domains as itemised above; the overall picture is concerning for early-onset sepsis and warrants prompt empiric treatment.

DRIVER BREAKDOWN:
- Maternal GBS colonization: GBS positive (+2 pts, layer 1, ~20.0% of total)
- Prolonged rupture of membranes: ROM 25.0h (>=18h) (+2 pts, layer 1, ~20.0% of total)
- Maternal intrapartum fever: Maternal temp 38.5C (+2 pts, layer 1, ~20.0% of total)
- Respiratory distress: Moderate respiratory distress (+2 pts, layer 2, ~20.0% of total)
- Elevated CRP: CRP 28.2 mg/L (+2 pts, layer 3, ~20.0% of total)

RECOMMENDED ACTIONS:
- Initiate empiric antibiotics within 1 hour per NICE guidance.
- Obtain blood culture before first antibiotic dose where not already drawn.
- Escalate to senior neonatal review and consider NICU-level monitoring.
